boundary_certificate.scope: Integer inequalities plus valuation/root argument; not machine-checked C++ control-flow proof.

actual_arm.reference: Exact rational decomposition, direct integer nth-root search and arbitrary-size powers. Fraction conversion supplies RNE; no floating log/exp/pow reference is used.

added: Signed operand aliases and truncating signed quotient/remainder.
Operand alias coherence, result-register writes and DIRTY handling for SDK context restoration.
Local latency checks remain attached to the issuing kernel; a later SDK save of an old pending result is handled separately.
sio_model.initial_failure: The first new boundary audit stopped on an unsupported signed SIO operand write. This was a verifier coverage gap; after extending and independently checking the model, the same firmware passed.
sio_model.hardware_model_scope: Functional model; own divider latency is separately checked. SDK wrapper IRQ injection is not modeled.

sources.finding: The paper explains why exact values and midpoints must be separated from adaptive nonboundary evaluation.
SIO operand aliases, signed results, writable result registers and quotient-read DIRTY acknowledgement.

limitations: Finite actual ARM cases complement the mathematical detector argument; they are not exhaustive verification over all input pairs.
Boundary recognition is now directly exercised; it does not establish a precision bound for nonboundary pow results.
The owned512/1024bit refinement still ends with an explicit undecided trap. Universal pow totality and the overall goal remain open.
V64 has not been measured on hardware; the previous full V60 comparison retains21strict slower groups. No ROOT math promotion or commit.
